findings.title: The predecessor role states that v1 measured a 'named-catalog' obligation. v1 has no such obligation, and no G23 named-corpus catalog artifact exists anywhere — G23's naming rests directly on the live harness cell, which is the distinction this gate's own OBL-G23-NAMED-CORPUS exists to record

measured.predecessorObligations: Frozen v1's obligation ids are OBL-G23-HARNESS-SPEC, OBL-G23-NAMED-CORPUS, OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING, OBL-G23-EXECUTION and OBL-NT35-UNNAMED-REMAINDER-CLOSED. There is no obligation containing 'catalog'.
measured.noCatalogArtifactExists: glob over docs/coop/artifacts for any g23 catalog returns nothing. G12, G19, G20, G21 and G22 each have a named-corpus catalog artifact; G23 does not.
measured.whatActuallyClosesTheNaming: OBL-G23-NAMED-CORPUS, in both v1 and v2, rests on the live harness cell: its reason reads 'G23 v1 namedCorpusNotAuthored carries one live harness-cell corpus phrase' and its existingGate is 'none. Live harness-cell naming only.'
measured.abbreviationStyleMakesItSpecific: The same sentence abbreviates two other real ids — 'harness-spec' for OBL-G23-HARNESS-SPEC and 'FX-AUTHORING' for OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING. Both map exactly. The middle term does not map to anything, which is what makes it a specific claim about v1's contents rather than a loose category label.
measured.soleOccurrence: 'catalog' occurs exactly once in the entire artifact, and that occurrence is this one.
measured.textIsNewInV2: Frozen v1 has no predecessor pin, so this role text appears for the first time in v2. It is not a sentence I saw and declined to charge in the previous cycle.

findings.likelyOrigin: The identical sentence appears in g19-leftover-join.v2's predecessor role, where it is accurate — G19 does have OBL-G19-NAMED-CATALOG and a real g19-named-corpus-catalog.v1 artifact, both of which I verified in that review. The template was carried across gates without adjusting for G23, which is the one gate in this family whose naming layer has no catalog.
findings.whyItMatters: It asserts a layer of the G23 chain that does not exist. A coordinator reading the predecessor role would expect a G23 catalog artifact to have been authored and measured, and would either go looking for a file that was never written or conclude that the naming close rests on a catalog when it rests on the live register cell. G23 is precisely the gate where that distinction is load-bearing, and the artifact records it correctly everywhere except here.
findings.whatIsNotWrong: No standing is affected. The naming layer is measured leftoverDesign false either way, under the correctly named OBL-G23-NAMED-CORPUS, whose own reason is accurate. Nothing is closed, authorized or minted by this error. It is a provenance-description inaccuracy, the same class as CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1, and it is why this is a SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
findings.fix: Replace 'named-catalog' with 'named-corpus' in basedOn.predecessor.role, matching the obligation v1 actually carries. Optionally also name OBL-NT35-UNNAMED-REMAINDER-CLOSED, which v1 likewise measured false and the role omits — though that omission alone is not charged, since the role does not claim to be exhaustive.

I did not charge them. They are denials of something the artifact indeed does not do, so nothing is asserted falsely and nothing is left undecidable; they are inert rather than wrong. Noted only because they are the same kind of cross-gate template carry-over that produced the finding above — in that case the carry-over asserted something, and that is what made the difference.

This is a successor rather than a fix-fold: the predecessor was ACCEPT 0/0, so no finding was outstanding. v2 adds OBL-G23-INPUT-CORPUS because g23-input-corpus.v1 became available and accepted. The addition itself is clean — scoped to naming, correctly bucketed, and it leaves FX-AUTHORING's standing untouched.

The finding is narrow and costs one word to fix, but it is worth stating why I charged a role field here and declined to charge one in a different chain earlier this session. There I declined because the sentence was true, made no exclusivity claim, and was unchanged from a version I had already reviewed without charging it. Here the sentence is new to v2, and it is false rather than merely incomplete: it names an obligation the predecessor does not have, in a gate that has no catalog at all.
The chain is single-reviewer end to end — no Codex artifact exists for the G23 harness, the input corpus, or either leftover-join version. All three verdict pins are Claude verdicts and one is mine.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: One SHOULD-FIX, no blockers. Both register checks pass by == against a DR-G23 row parsed into all eight cells before the subject was opened: liveGateOwners.DR-G23 is 'Protocol + semantic owners', equal to live owner cell [4] and to the pinned G23 v1 harness, and file08StatusToken is OPEN. The NT prohibition is fully honoured — NT-1, NT-2, NT-4, NT-6, NT-7 and NT-8 occur only inside denial sentences and are never given a name, input or corpus role, while NT-3 and NT-5 are the gate's legitimate classes; D-147's stale cardinalities of 18, 19 and 20 are also absent against a live 26. What lands is in basedOn.predecessor.role, which says v1 'Measured harness-spec and named-catalog leftoverDesign false.' Frozen v1 has no catalog obligation — its id is OBL-G23-NAMED-CORPUS — and no G23 catalog artifact exists anywhere, unlike G12, G19, G20, G21 and G22. G23's naming rests directly on the live harness cell, which is exactly what OBL-G23-NAMED-CORPUS records. The sentence abbreviates two other real ids correctly, which is what makes the middle term a specific claim rather than a loose label, and 'catalog' occurs exactly once in the whole file — here. The identical sentence is accurate in g19-leftover-join.v2, so this reads as a template carried across gates without adjusting for the one gate that has no catalog. It is new text in v2, not something I saw and passed on in the previous cycle. No standing is affected and the fix is one word. Everything else is clean: 9 of 9 basedOn pins and 10 of 10 recordedInputs recompute, all three cited verdicts are genuinely ACCEPT 0/0, the corpus phrase equals live G23 v1 by ==, D-147's closure is quoted accurately against live COORD, the D-146 relationship matches the harness's own leftoverNameNote, and the diff against v1 shows four obligations byte-identical, one new, one changed in its reason alone. 19 attacks run, 18 refuted, one landing.
